messages:
alyssa: Heads-up — billing pinged about a huge GPU charge spike this morning, looks like ~$36k extra in the last 3 hrs. :grimacing:
mike: yikes. did we get a report from autoscaler or cloud?
sean: Checking cluster logs now. I see a bunch of Karpenter provisioner events at 08:12 UTC — it launched 48 nodes across us-west-2, most are on-demand g5.12xlarge.
alyssa: Wait, we intended spot preference. Why on-demand?
sean: The provisioner picked LT-ml-gpu-v2 which has mixed-instance but the launch template override has CapacityType=ON_DEMAND for a subset. Looks like a previous emergency patch left that in place.
mike: ugh. any pods failing to schedule before that?
sean: Yep — a batch of pod pending logs show tolerations/taints mismatch for the spot-only nodegroup. Karpenter tried to satisfy with on-demand capacity instead.
infra-oncall: I just ran `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=instance-type,Values=g5.12xlarge --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].[InstanceId,Placement,InstanceLifecycle]'` — returning a lot of instances with InstanceLifecycle null (on-demand).
jen: Billing-bot recorded the spike: "2026-03-18 08:15 — On-demand GPU spend jump: $36,140 for us-west-2 within 180m".
alyssa: Immediate mitigation: 1) scale down the launch template overrides to zero for on-demand; 2) cordon + drain on-demand GPU nodes not serving long-running jobs; 3) set Karpenter TTL to be aggressive. Sean, can you handle the drains?
sean: On it. Running `kubectl get nodes -l instance-type=g5.12xlarge` then `kubectl drain` for nodes with no critical pods.
mike: Also open a billing dispute / support ticket — ask for retroactive credits, mention misconfiguration and rapid autoscale. Jen can you file?
jen: Filing ticket now with cloud support. Attaching autoscaler events and launch template diff. Ticket ref: AWS-9876123.
infra-oncall: Note: reserve commitments (savings plans/reserved instances) won't cover these unexpected on-demand hours. This eats into our budget. We should consider a small buffer in Dedicated capacity for peak fallback.
alyssa: Agreed — we need a postmortem with remediation: a) remove on-demand override from LT; b) add pre-deploy lint in infra CI to reject CapacityType=ON_DEMAND in GPU LTs; c) autoscaler policy change to prefer spot and limit on-demand fallback to N nodes/day; d) alert for >$5k/hr GPU burn.
sean: Drains complete for 30 nodes; 18 remain active with important training jobs. Karpenter is resyncing and provisioning spot g5s now.
mike: What's the expected burn for the remainder of the day?
jen: Based on current node mix, projected extra on-demand delta drops to ~$2.3k over next 24h if no further failures. I'll add this to the ticket.
alyssa: Good. Also schedule a short ops runbook update: how to flip LT capacity types and test on staging. Assign owners.
sean: I'll push a quick PR to terraform to fix the launch template and add a lint. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
mike: Postmortem owner?
alyssa: Sean will own immediate remediation and the postmortem. Jen will own billing follow-up. Infra-oncall will propose commit/reserved capacity sizing for GPU pool and run a cost/benefit analysis next week.
jen: Added tasks to #incidents board.
billing-bot: Automated note — billing ticket AWS-9876123 created; case updated with logs and request for service credits.
alyssa: Thanks team. Lessons: small infra patches can have big dollar consequences. We'll track follow-ups in the postmortem. :memo: 
sean: one more note — add a guard in Karpenter provisioning policy: max on-demand GPUs per cluster = 4. I'll include that in the PR.
